newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX natgas pares gains late, fronts lose ground.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX natgas pares gains late, fronts lose ground.

text.p: NYMEX Hub natgas futures pared morning gains and turned mixed late Monday, hit by some technical selling when an early short covering rally on firmer cash prices stalled at resistance, industry sources said.
At 1425 EST, April eased 2.7 cents to $1.92 per million British thermal units after stalling early at $2.04. May was 1.3 cents lower at $2.01. Most others were up slightly.
"We had a lot of short covering early and then it dried up and locals started bailing out of length," said one New York-based futures trader.
Despite colder East Coast weather this week that helped firm the early Monday cash, traders said ample storage and the approach of spring should mean any rally will be short-lived near-term.

Technical traders said an early flood of speculative buying and short covering, particularly when April pierced psychological resistance at $2, seemed to run out of steam this afternoon. Resistance was still pegged at $2.04 and then in the mid-teens. Support was seen at $1.78-1.80 and then at the $1.701 contract low.

In the cash, Gulf Coast prices firmed almost five cents Monday to the low-$1.90s. Midcon pipes were talked up slightly in the high-$1.70s. New York city gate swing gas gained more than five cents to the low-$2.20s on colder weather there.
Hub open interest on March 7 rose 3,509 lots to 169,158.
NYMEX Alberta and Permian natgas were untraded at 1415 EST.
On the KCBT, April slipped two cents to $1.70, while deferreds were steady to up nine cents. The East/West spread narrowed by 0.7 cent to 22.0 cents (NYMEX premium).
